fixes: Anchor Date Investigation — HR stat pill showed misleading daily average when intraday swing >= 20 bpm. Root cause: bpSeries('h') computes the daily mean of all readings; a day with 68→91→68 BPM averaged to ~76 bpm, completely hiding the spike in the 'On target date' pill. Fix: after computing hrAnchor (daily avg), the raw HR readings for the anchor date are also scanned for min/max. When max−min >= 20 bpm (matching the Rapid HR Change detector threshold exactly), the 'On target date' pill shows 'low→high bpm' labeled 'On target date (range)' instead of the average. Threshold of 20 bpm is clinically grounded — it is the same gate the rapid change detector uses, so the two systems are always in agreement.

Anchor Date Investigation — summary text showed the same misleading daily-average HR when intraday swing >= 20 bpm. generateAnchorSummaryText() now re-derives min/max from raw readings for the anchor date and, when swing >= 20 bpm, emits 'Heart rate on anchor date ranged from X to Y bpm (intraday swing of Z bpm). Prior 14-day average was N bpm.' instead of the averaged value.
